events.description: I write articles on a variety of topics, sharing insights and experiences with a broader audience. My Medium profile features pieces on technology, education, and personal growth, reflecting my diverse interests and commitment to accessible content creation.
Every Sunday, I lead experiments and learning plans for visitors ranging from young children to adults in the Charles River Yawkey Gallery and the Engineering Design Workshop.
I research, write, and collaborate on local journalism pieces covering town events and school news. Meeting deadlines for hyperlocal coverage is its own particular discipline!

I tutor K–9 students in math, adjusting lessons to individual needs and writing detailed session reports for families. I'm certified in Mathnasium Methods, which sounds more impressive than it probably is (a test on addition and subtraction), but the tutoring itself I take seriously.
I’m helping plan Campfire Boston, a game jam hackathon for high schoolers interested in CS. My responsibilities include contacting venues, coordinating sponsors, and handling marketing.
I completed five certificates focused on Data Science and AI, working on projects that spotlighted women in STEM and deepened my understanding of AI's errors and useful applications across careers.

I work with Computer Science professors using Jupyter notebooks to analyze large datasets on how algorithms affect youth behavior across Instagram and Facebook. The data is unsurprising in the bad ways and surprising in the good ways!

I contribute to ongoing research on local, state, and federal elections in support of non-partisan political coverage. I'm in high school doing this, which I guess I find impressive enough to mention.

I pursue goals across volunteer service, personal development, physical fitness, and exploration under the Congressional Award framework. In December 2025, I was awarded the Gold Certificate for reaching requirements across all four pillars.

I collaborated on engineering projects involving soldering, Raspberry Pi, embedded systems in machine code, and prototype building using woodworking and advanced design techniques. I came in not knowing exactly how to solder. I left knowing exactly how to solder!

events.organization: The Academies by Harvard Student Agencies
events.description: I participated in mock consulting projects, analyzing cases, presenting team solutions, and building skills through hands-on practice. It's essentially a simulation of something that will one day have much higher stakes.
I draft grant proposals, plan community events, and identify strategic growth opportunities with the team!
I participate in civic education, political organizing, and peer collaboration on democratic issues at the high school level. I show up, which already puts me ahead of most eligible voters.

I attend seminars and discussions on economic policy, engaging with professionals and staying informed on policy impacts through expert-led sessions. A lot of it goes over my head, which is precisely the point.
I participated in Kode With Klossy's Code-A-Bration, an event celebrating women and girls in coding and technology.

I reviewed, edited, and wrote policy articles addressing social, political, and economic issues, tailoring content for clarity and accessibility for youth audiences. Three months of this taught me that 'accessible' is harder to write than 'technical.'

I completed an intensive summer program in foundational computer science, gaining hands-on experience with programming, algorithms, and problem-solving through team-based projects. It was the summer I decided I actually liked coding!

roles.description: I contribute to educational digitization and enrichment projects remotely. It's quieter than my other commitments, which I appreciate.
I support museum programs and engage visitors in hands-on science activities.
I transcribe historical documents to make them accessible for researchers.

awards.title: Congressional Award Gold Certificate
awards.description: I was awarded for reaching requirements in Personal Development, Physical Development, Exploration, and Volunteership.

awards.title: DECA State Qualifier (1st place)
awards.description: I placed 1st out of roughly 40 individuals in MA District 10 in the Business Finance Series event. I scored an 84/100 on the exam and a 93/100 on the roleplay. The roleplay is the part I'm more willing to brag about.

awards.title: Athena Award
awards.description: I was awarded for completing the Athena Award Program, held in collaboration with MIT, the U.S. Congressional App Challenge, Girls Who Code, and GitHub. I shipped 7 projects representing 30 hours of work. The certificate recognizes independent project development and contributions to Hack Club's global community of young creators.

awards.title: MASCO Finalist (4th place)
awards.description: I qualified for the Massachusetts Computer Science Olympiad in-person finals. 4th place is not 1st place, but I did make it to finals, which is its own thing.

awards.title: DECA State Qualifier (5th place)
awards.description: I placed top 5 out of roughly 30 teams in MA District 10 in the Financial Team Decision Making event. Our team scored a composite 72/100 on the exam and an 87/100 on the roleplay. Again, the roleplay.
